n:Government of Argentina (Treasury): The Treasury is the part of Argentina's government in Buenos Aires that manages public spending, and it is tied to the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic (BCRA). In May 2023, an election year, the BCRA transferred another 140 billion Argentine pesos to the Treasury through temporary advances, which are short-term loans of newly created money. Transfers since March reached 370 billion pesos, which used 99.2% of the 372.8 billion peso first-half limit that Argentina had agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
n:Council of Representatives of Iraq (co: This is a committee of Iraq's parliament, in Baghdad, tied to the Central Bank of Iraq. In 2012 it investigated the bank over possible manipulation of the dinar against the dollar and charged that bank officials were abusing the bank's dollar sales. In October 2012 the cabinet removed governor al-Shabibi, and the Supreme Judicial Council confirmed arrest warrants for him and other officials without giving the charges. His defence called the case politically motivated.
n:PricewaterhouseCoopers: PricewaterhouseCoopers is an accounting firm based in London, United Kingdom. It is named in a case involving the Central Bank of Somalia. A July 2013 report by the UN Monitoring Group for Somalia and Eritrea said 80 percent of the bank's withdrawals were for private purposes and that the governor was key to irregularities. It said 12 million dollars of 16.9 million dollars transferred by PricewaterhouseCoopers could not be traced. The central bank rejected the allegations.
n:Absa: Absa is a bank based in Johannesburg, South Africa. It is tied to the South African Reserve Bank, the country's central bank, through an apartheid-era rescue loan the Reserve Bank gave to another bank, Bankorp. In June 2017 the Public Protector, a South African state watchdog, ordered Absa to repay 1.125 billion rand for that rescue. On 16 February 2018 the Pretoria High Court set aside the Public Protector's report and its orders, after the Reserve Bank and Absa asked for a review. The court also ordered the Public Protector to pay part of the Reserve Bank's costs personally.
n:State Tribunal (Poland): The State Tribunal is a court in Warsaw. It is tied to the National Bank of Poland through a motion that members of parliament from the governing coalition filed on 26 March 2024 to bring the bank's president, Adam Glapiński, before it. The motion lists eight charges, including bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and currency interventions carried out without authorization. These are accusations, and no ruling by the Tribunal is recorded.
n:Attorney-General of Libya: The Attorney-General of Libya is tied to the Central Bank of Libya through a forged banknote complaint. In November 2022 the central bank accused its deputy governor, Ali al-Hibri, of signing forged 50-dinar banknotes it said were printed in Russia and bore his signature. Governor Saddek Elkaber asked the Attorney-General to pursue a complaint. The bank did not say how many notes were involved. No response from al-Hibri and no later outcome are reported, so the accusation is unproven.
n:Parliamentary inquiry commission on No: This is a Portuguese parliamentary commission, based in Lisbon, that investigated the losses of Novo Banco. It is tied to the Bank of Portugal, the central bank, as its investigator. On 20 July 2021 the commission's rapporteur, Fernando Anastácio, presented a proposed final report saying supervision failed across the board and that there was a permanent and systematic failure. This was a draft. The PSD party said its deputies would vote against it and propose amendments.
n:Cristina Kirchner: Cristina Kirchner was President of Argentina. She is tied to the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic through the removal of its governor, Martin Redrado. On 6 January the government called on him to resign, saying he refused to back its decree calling for 6.6 billion dollars of reserves. He refused to go. On 7 January Kirchner issued a second decree firing him and accusing him of misconduct. On 8 January the courts suspended both decrees.
n:Directorate of Public Prosecutions (Bo: The Directorate of Public Prosecutions of Botswana is the state prosecuting body. A woman arrested on 17 October 2019 was implicated, with others including former president Ian Khama and former intelligence head Isaac Kgosi, in allegedly stealing 100 billion pula from the Bank of Botswana. High Court Judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and a false passport declaration. The state withdrew a terrorism financing charge. He found the accusations fabricated and referred the investigator to police for perjury prosecution.
JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., a bank in New York that is part of JPMorgan Chase & Co., owns 60,600,000 shares, 29.5%, of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, part of the US Federal Reserve System, as of 31 December 2018. Here a shareholder owns part of the central bank. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:Goldman Sachs Bank USA: Goldman Sachs Bank USA, a bank in New York that is part of The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., owns 8,300,000 shares, 4.0%, of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, part of the US Federal Reserve System, as of 31 December 2018. Here a shareholder owns part of the central bank. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., a bank in New York that is part of Morgan Stanley, owns 4,800,000 shares in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, part of the US Federal Reserve System, as of 31 December 2018. Here a shareholder owns part of the central bank. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. The article gives 3.7% combined for the two Morgan Stanley entities, not separately.
Morgan Stanley Private Bank, N.A., a bank in New York that is part of Morgan Stanley, owns 2,800,000 shares in the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, part of the US Federal Reserve System, as of 31 December 2018. Here a shareholder owns part of the central bank. At the Federal Reserve, member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors; since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president. Combined with Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. the article gives 3.7%.
n:Absa Bank Limited: Absa Bank Limited is a bank based in Johannesburg, South Africa. It is a shareholder of the South African Reserve Bank, meaning it owns part of the central bank. It holds 10,000 shares, 0.5% of the total, as of 30 June 2022. This figure comes from a secondary source, a news article citing the Reserve Bank's shareholder index, and has not been checked against a primary source.
n:UBS Group AG: UBS Group AG is a firm based in Zurich, Switzerland. It is tied to the Group of Thirty, a forum where central bankers also sit. Gail Kelly represents the firm there as member of the Board of Directors.
n:The Northern Trust Company (Northern T: The Northern Trust Company (Northern Trust Corp.), based in Chicago, United States, is a member bank of the Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, and owns shares in it. It holds $70,000,000 of stock in the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago (2025 average balance). Member banks that hold a Reserve Bank's shares elect six of its nine directors (Class A and B); since 2010 the bankers' three Class A directors no longer vote on choosing its president.
n:AKO Capital LLP: AKO Capital LLP is an investment firm in London. Nicolai Tangen, the incoming chief executive of the fund arm of Norges Bank, Norway's central bank, had a holding in it. In August 2020, after the Storting's finance committee raised conflict-of-interest concerns, the bank's board rewrote his terms: he would give up that holding and transfer it and its dividend rights to the charitable AKO Foundation, with no ownership interest in perpetuity. Supervisory Board chair Julie Brodtkorb said guidelines, regulations and laws had been breached in the appointment. Tangen took office on 1 September.
n:Supreme Court of Thailand, Criminal Di: This division of Thailand's Supreme Court, in Bangkok, tries people who have held political office. It convicted former finance minister Surapong Suebwonglee of malfeasance under Section 157 of the Criminal Code for appointing Sathit Limpongpan, Vijit Supinij and Chaiwat Wibulsawasdi in 2008 to the committee that selects members of the Bank of Thailand's board; all three were representatives of financial institutions under Bank of Thailand supervision. He was given one year in jail, suspended for one year, and a fine of 20,000 baht. The National Anti-Corruption Commission had filed the case on 27 May 2015.
n:Sejm of the Republic of Poland: The Sejm is the lower house of Poland's parliament, in Warsaw, and it was asked to put the country's central bank chief on trial. The ruling coalition accused National Bank of Poland governor Glapinski of breaking several laws and of failing to uphold the bank's political independence, and in March 2024 moved to bring him before the State Tribunal. On 20 August 2024 the Constitutional Tribunal ruled that law unconstitutional. It had already held, on 12 January 2024, that 276 of the 460 seats were needed; the coalition had 241.
n:ING Bank: A bank based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Valeria Gontareva worked there before she became Governor of the National Bank of Ukraine in 2014, though the source naming the firm gives no role or years.
n:Northern Trust Company: The Northern Trust Company is a bank in Chicago, United States. J. Charles Partee worked there before joining the Federal Reserve. He went from Northern Trust Company of Chicago to the Fed's staff and then to a seat on its Board of Governors, which he held from 5 January 1976 to 7 February 1986. After that he joined the board of State Farm Insurance and took a mutual fund trusteeship.
Bear Stearns & Co., Inc. was an investment bank in New York. Wayne D. Angell taught economics at Ottawa University in Kansas from 1956 to 1985, sat in the Kansas House of Representatives from 1960 to 1966, and was an officer and director of several banks in Kansas and Missouri from 1971 to 1985. He was a Governor of the Federal Reserve Board from 7 February 1986 until he retired on 2 February 1994, after which he became chief economist at Bear Stearns.
n:ING Group: ING Group is a bank, marked in the United States. Robert P. Forrestal became president and chief executive officer of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta on 7 December 1983 and served until 1 January 1996. After retiring from the bank he worked with the Atlanta law firm Smith, Gambrell & Russell and sat on several corporate boards, among them ING North America Co. and the ING Advisory Council in the Netherlands, as well as Equifax Inc. and Genuine Parts Co. He died in 2004. No ethics finding is recorded.
n:AIA Group Limited: AIA Group Limited is a publicly listed pan-Asian life insurance group based in Hong Kong. It is linked to one central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, through a person who worked for both. Tan Sri Mohamed Azman Yahya was an independent non-executive director of the insurer from 24 February 2014 to 28 May 2020, and joined Bank Negara Malaysia's Board of Directors on 1 June 2020, four days after leaving.
n:Board of Supreme Audit: The Board of Supreme Audit is Iraq's state audit body; the map places its marker on the country rather than the exact office. It audits the accounts of the Central Bank of Iraq, a role set out in the central bank law issued as Coalition Provisional Authority Order Number 56 in 2004.
n:Standard Chartered Bank: Standard Chartered Bank is a bank based in London. It stores gold for Bangladesh Bank, the central bank of Bangladesh: reporting of 8 September 2026 on where those reserves sit said that as of June Standard Chartered held 92,739 troy ounces of Bangladesh Bank's gold, worth around 45.66 billion taka, in the United Kingdom. That is custody of a reserve asset, not management of the bank's money.
n:Münze Österreich AG (Austrian Mint), V: The Austrian Mint is owned by the central bank and stores gold for it. The Oesterreichische Nationalbank says 50 tons of its gold sit in the vaults of Münze Österreich AG, one of its own subsidiaries. That is part of the 140 tons the bank keeps inside Austria, out of 280 tons in total, so a company the bank owns holds more than a third of the gold Austria keeps at home.
n:JPMorgan Chase Bank: JPMorgan Chase Bank is a commercial bank. It appears here as a place where a central bank keeps gold: the Bank of Mongolia's audited accounts for 2021 say its monetary gold and silver are mainly placed at the Bank of England and at JPMorgan Chase Bank. That is worth noticing, because most gold custody on this map is held by other central banks or by a bank's own vaults, and a commercial bank holding a central bank's gold is a different kind of arrangement. Holding is not managing: a bank that keeps gold as a depository does not own it.
